name: street-tenor-horn-stabs
style: East Coast boom-bap, 1997 New York, 90 BPM, patient countdown rap. Picture a freezing corner past 2 a.m., steam rising off a grate, everyone watching everyone: tense, sly, quietly menacing. One brooding two-second chop of muted brass over minor strings, lifted off dusty vinyl, punches once at each number then pulls back. Thick knocking kick, a snare that cracks like a slammed door, lazy swung hats, deep round bass, crackle in the grooves. Rapper: young street tenor, high and nasal with rasp in the throat, barking with corner-boy confidence, every syllable clipped and placed, never hurried. He drops the number, lets it hang for a breath, then delivers the rule. In each gap the turntablist chirps and baby-scratches a short wordless cut. For the closing fix, the sample and bass vanish and the voice rides the kick and snare by itself.
exclude: sung hook, crooning, choir, autotune, trap hi-hat rolls, 808 glides, EDM build, rapid-fire flow, female voice, gang chant
lyrics:
[Intro: brass-and-strings chop hits once, kick and snare fall in, cold and sly]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Instrumental: quick chirp scratches, no vocals]

[Verse: punchy, deliberate, one bar per line; number alone on the beat, a breath, then the line]
Rule number Uno: never say how much you made,
doesn't matter anyway, since the gold went away.

[Instrumental: baby scratch cut, no vocals]

[brass stab on the number]
Number two: never show 'em your next move,
cut the rate for the banks, hike it when you land.

[Instrumental: short transformer scratch, no vocals]

[brass stab on the number]
Number three: never trust nobody with the press,
before Bernie gets made off face loss.

[Instrumental: chirp scratches, no vocals]

[brass stab on the number]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Instrumental: baby scratch cut, no vocals]

[brass stab on the number]
Number five: never print where you sleep,
never let them owe the oats you reap.

[Instrumental: quick scratch fill, no vocals]

[brass stab on the number]
Number six: no credit? Forget it,
let the junkie know you better forget that.

[Instrumental: slow drag scratch, no vocals]

[brass stab, softer, voice lowered]
Seven, and nobody says it out loud:
keep your money and your assets apart, not in one crowd.

[Instrumental: chirp scratches, no vocals]

[brass stab on the number]
Number eight: hold none of it yourself,
debase 'em till the numbers go through.

[Instrumental: stuttered scratch, no vocals]

[brass stab, sly and knowing]
Nine's the one they'd rather you skipped:
keep the auditors out, sporadic trips and you out.

[Instrumental: double scratch cut, no vocals]

[brass stab, the hardest one]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout in stride and they ain't paid it all.

[Outro: sample and bass cut out, kick and snare only; plain, unhurried]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End]
